summary: 高帝侄，废郁林、海陵自立；建武年间大诛高武诸子，史称惨毒；孝文帝南伐齐边告急，永泰元年崩。
summary_en: Nephew of Emperor Gao, he deposed the Prince of Yulin and the Prince of Hailing to take the throne; in the Jianwu years he slaughtered the sons of Gaodi and Wudi — the histories call it poison; Emperor Xiaowen of Wei marched south and the border was in peril. He died in the 1st year of Yongtai.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现阴鸷多忌的君主之态，衣冠从南齐中制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 始安贞王道生子，字景栖。
timeline.summary_en: Son of Xiao Daosheng, Prince Zhen of Shian, styled Jingqi.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary_en: He deposed the Prince of Hailing, took the throne himself, and changed the era to Jianwu.

timeline.title: 大诛宗室
timeline.summary: 剪除高帝、武帝诸子，史称惨毒。
timeline.summary_en: He cut down the sons of Emperor Gao and Emperor Wu — the histories call it poison.

timeline.title: 魏军南伐
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei marched south, and the Qi border was in peril.

timeline.title: 明帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩，子宝卷继，是为东昏侯。
timeline.summary_en: He died; his son Baojuan succeeded — the Marquis of Donghun.

timeline.title: 明帝总评
timeline.summary: 有吏干而多猜忌，骨肉相残。
timeline.summary_en: Competent in administration but steeped in jealousy — kin slaying kin.

bio_md:
# 齐明帝 · 主要事迹

萧鸾字景栖，高帝侄，始安贞王萧道生之子。仕宋、齐两朝，以宗室之尊、吏干之才历任要职。建武元年，鸾废海陵王自立，改元建武——齐之高武子孙，从此尽在刀俎。明帝在位四年，「大诛宗室」：高帝十九子、武帝诸子，杀之殆尽，「高武子孙，遂无遗类」，史称其「惨毒」。

明帝之治，尚有吏干：整顿户籍、核实户口、减免赋役，政事颇有条理；建武四年，北魏孝文帝大举南伐，明帝遣军拒之，齐边告急而未致大败。然其猜忌成性，「深自藏匿」，以「典签」监视诸王，暮年尤甚，因无子而密令宠妃「代育」——骨肉相残，无所不用其极。

永泰元年，明帝崩，年四十七，子萧宝卷（东昏侯）即位。史评明帝：「有吏才而多猜忌，以诛戮为威。」萧鸾以宗室篡立、屠戮高武子孙，虽一时得逞，然其子东昏侯暴虐更甚，萧衍起兵，不过三年而齐亡——明帝之「惨毒」，实为齐祚速亡之直接原因。

> 参考：点校本《南齐书》卷006《明帝纪》、卷035《高帝诸子传》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Luan, styled Jingqi, was a nephew of Emperor Gao, son of Xiao Daosheng, Prince Zhen of Shian. Serving both Song and Qi, he held the highest offices as a senior prince of tested ability. In the 1st year of Jianwu he deposed the Prince of Hailing and took the throne himself — and from that day the sons of Gao and Wu were under the knife. Four years he reigned, "slaughtering the princes": of Gao's nineteen sons and Wu's sons, nearly all were destroyed, "so that no descendant of Gao and Wu remained" — the histories call it poison.

Yet he had administrative talent: he revised the registers, verified the households, lightened the levies, and kept the government in order; in the 4th year of Jianwu, when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei marched south in force, he held the line and the border, though in peril, did not break. But his jealousy was a disease: "hiding himself deep," he set the secretaries of inspection over the princes, and in his last years, having no son, had his favorites "bear children" for him — the family cruelty carried to its last extreme.

He died in the 1st year of Yongtai at forty-seven; his son Baojuan, the Marquis of Donghun, succeeded. The histories say: "administrative ability with boundless jealousy, ruling by slaughter." A senior prince who usurped and butchered the sons of Gao and Wu, he held his throne a while — but his son's tyranny was worse, Xiao Yan rose, and within three years Qi was gone: his "poison" was the direct cause of the realm's swift fall.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Ming"), ch. 35 (biographies of Gao's sons).
